literary-1.title: Literary Collection I
literary-1.description: A collection of atmospheric presets inspired by the characters, settings, and shadowed worlds of Jane Austen, Charles Dickens, F. Scott Fitzgerald, and Edgar Allan Poe.
literary-1.menuImageAlt: A menu card representing Literary Collection I.

presets.title: Dashwood
presets.author: Jane Austen
presets.quote: “To be unaffected was all that a pretty girl could want to make her mind as captivating as her person.”
presets.alt: Moss-covered stone arch bridge over a flowing woodland stream surrounded by dense green trees.

presets.title: Fanny
presets.author: Jane Austen
presets.quote: “She was beyond their reach; and if at last obliged to yield—no matter—it was all misery now.”
presets.alt: Woman in a white period dress seated by a window, holding a book and looking outside.

presets.title: Highbury
presets.author: Jane Austen
presets.quote: “A very few to-morrows stood between the young people of Highbury and happiness.”
presets.alt: Two men in white shirts stand behind a woman in a period dress and pearls in a green outdoor setting.

presets.title: Longbourn
presets.author: Jane Austen
presets.quote: “Anything beyond the very neighbourhood of Longbourn, I suppose, would appear far.”
presets.alt: Large gray stone manor house with tall windows, hedges, and lawn beneath an overcast sky.

presets.title: Tilney
presets.author: Jane Austen
presets.quote: “He was rather tall, had a pleasing countenance, a very intelligent and lively eye, and, if not quite handsome, was very near it.”
presets.alt: Man in dark period clothing and a broad hat riding a black horse along a rugged coast with ruins.

presets.title: Chesney Wold
presets.author: Charles Dickens
presets.quote: “Howls the shrill wind round Chesney Wold; the sharp rain beats, the windows rattle, and the chimneys growl.”
presets.alt: Woman in an elaborate black Victorian dress standing in an ornate teal room lit by candles.

presets.title: Dotheboys
presets.author: Charles Dickens
presets.quote:
“The walls were so stained
and discoloured, that it was impossible to tell whether they had
ever been touched with paint or whitewash.”
presets.alt: Symmetrical red-brick historic courtyard with a central clock tower beneath a blue sky.

presets.title: Gradgrind
presets.author: Charles Dickens
presets.quote: “A man of realities... ready to weigh and measure any parcel of human nature, and tell you exactly what it comes to.”
presets.alt: Close side-profile portrait of a bearded man wearing a tall hat and fur-trimmed coat.

presets.title: Havisham
presets.author: Charles Dickens
presets.quote: “I saw that the bride within the bridal dress had withered like the dress, and like the flowers, and had no brightness left but the brightness of her sunken eyes.”
presets.alt: Dark, weathered ornamental wall partly covered by shadowy dried foliage and flowers.

presets.title: Tattycoram
presets.author: Charles Dickens
presets.quote: “And this is how Tattycoram will be a greater traveller in course of time than Captain Cook.”
presets.alt: Woman in a black dress and bonnet standing beside a leaf-strewn path under autumn trees.

presets.title: Gloria
presets.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
presets.quote: “Gloria was chewing an amazing gum-drop and staring moodily out the window.”
presets.alt: Man in a dark suit seated in an ornate chair with a woman in a black dress reclining across his lap.

presets.title: Myrtle
presets.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
presets.quote: “Myrtle raised her eyebrows in despair at the shiftlessness of the lower orders.”
presets.alt: Two women in 1920s-style dresses and feathered headbands pose together, one holding a cigarette holder.

presets.title: Rosalind
presets.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
presets.quote: “Always in a sort of breathless hush, as if they feared that any minute the spell would break and drop them out of this paradise of rose and flame.”
presets.alt: Woman in a white fur stole, pearls, and jeweled headband holding a long cigarette holder in a dark room.

presets.title: Valley of Ashes
presets.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
presets.quote: “A fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens”
presets.alt: Vintage black-and-beige automobile with whitewall tires parked on grass.

presets.title: West Egg
presets.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
presets.quote: “I drove into West Egg Village to search for her among soggy whitewashed alleys and to buy some cups and lemons and flowers.”
presets.alt: Grand white neoclassical mansion and formal lawn beneath a vivid blue sky.

presets.title: Dupin
presets.author: Edgar Allan Poe
presets.quote: “He ceased to bestir himself in the world, or to care for the retrieval of his fortunes.”
presets.quotefrom: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
presets.alt: Bearded man in a black cloak standing pensively beside a moss-covered stone wall in a misty woodland.

presets.title: Prospero
presets.author: Edgar Allan Poe
presets.quote: “He, having attained the extremity of the velvet apartment, turned suddenly and confronted his pursuer.”
presets.quotefrom: The Masque of the Red Death
presets.alt: Plague doctor near a white tent and a group of period-costumed figures in a castle courtyard.

presets.title: Roderick
presets.author: Edgar Allan Poe
presets.quote: “A cadaverousness of complexion; an eye large, liquid, and luminous beyond comparison.”
presets.quotefrom: The Fall of the House of Usher
presets.alt: Dark Gothic mansion among bare trees and green fog beneath an eerily illuminated sky.

presets.title: Rowena
presets.author: Edgar Allan Poe
presets.quote: “In her perturbed state of half-slumber, she spoke of sounds, and of motions, in and about the chamber of the turret.”
presets.alt: Shadowed figure in a pale gown holding a single lit candle.

presets.title: Weir
presets.author: Edgar Allan Poe
presets.quote: “It was down by the dank tarn of Auber, in the ghoul-haunted woodland of Weir.”
presets.alt: Cluster of deep red roses emerging from a nearly black background.

literary-2.title: Literary Collection II
literary-2.description: A second volume of literary presets inspired by the vivid people and places found in the writing of James Baldwin, Jack London, Herman Melville, and Edith Wharton.
literary-2.menuImageAlt: A menu card representing Literary Collection II.

presets.title: David
presets.author: James Baldwin
presets.quote: “What was strange was that this was but one tiny aspect of the dreadful human tangle, occurring everywhere, without end, forever.”
presets.alt: Two men kissing in a warmly lit bedroom beside a tall window.

presets.title: Fonny
presets.author: James Baldwin
presets.quote: “The train rocked, he held me closer, and a kind of sigh I'd never heard before stifled itself in him.”
presets.alt: Shirtless Black man wearing chains stands beneath a bright overhead light in a dark brick courtyard.

presets.title: Grimes
presets.author: James Baldwin
presets.quote: “In the eye there was a light that was not the light of Heaven, and the mouth trembled, lustful and lewd, to drink deep of the wines of Hell.”
presets.quotefrom: Go Tell It on the Mountain
presets.alt: Portrait of a Black man in a brown suit and brimmed hat against warm, blurred lights.

presets.title: Ida
presets.author: James Baldwin
presets.quote: “It was the way the world treated girls with bad reputations and every colored girl had been born with one.”
presets.alt: Elegantly dressed Black woman in a feathered hat looking toward the camera at a crowded evening gathering.

presets.title: Sonny
presets.author: James Baldwin
presets.quote: “I suppose this to mean that the song is still needed, still has work to do.”
presets.alt: Silhouetted guests and a pianist in a crowded nightclub glowing with red and orange light.

presets.title: Chechaquo
presets.author: Jack London
presets.quote: “The proper function of a man is to live, not to exist.”
presets.alt: Extreme close-up of a frost-covered person's face and outstretched hand amid blowing snow.

presets.title: Ghost
presets.author: Jack London
presets.quote: “He was not immoral, but merely unmoral.”
presets.alt: Two figures standing high in the rigging of a sailing ship surrounded by calm polar water and icebergs.

presets.title: Lizzie
presets.author: Jack London
presets.quote: “You belong to the legions of toil, with all that is low, and vulgar, and unbeautiful.”
presets.alt: Cropped view of a woman's hands and dark period dress while walking on a cobbled street.

presets.title: Pocket Miner
presets.author: Jack London
presets.quote: “If it ain’t the real thing, may God knock off my head with sour apples.”
presets.alt: Close-up of hands panning for gold in a shallow stream.

presets.title: Spitz
presets.author: Jack London
presets.quote: “Bitter rage was his, but never blind rage.”
presets.alt: White dog standing alone in deep snow beneath a pale sky.

presets.title: Aladdin's Palace
presets.author: Herman Melville
presets.quote: “All the mirrors and marbles around me seemed crawling over with lizards.”
presets.alt: Ornate empty bar with crystal chandeliers, shelves of bottles, and dramatic red and amber lighting.

presets.title: Bellipotent
presets.author: Herman Melville
presets.quote: “And good bye to you too, old Rights of Man.”
presets.alt: Silhouette of a three-masted sailing ship against a fiery orange sunset over the sea.

presets.title: Gingernut
presets.author: Herman Melville
presets.quote: “Indeed, to this quick-witted youth the whole noble science of the law was contained in a nut-shell.”
presets.alt: Freckled boy in a flat cap, white shirt, and suspenders standing in a crowd.

presets.title: Marnoo
presets.author: Herman Melville
presets.quote:
“The elegant outline of his figure, together with his
beardless cheeks, might have entitled him to the distinction of
standing for the statue of the Polynesian Apollo.”
presets.alt: Close-up portrait of a person with extensive black facial and neck tattoos against a dark background.

presets.title: Pequod
presets.author: Herman Melville
presets.quote: “A noble craft, but somehow a most melancholy! All noble things are touched with that.”
presets.alt: Close-up of wet wooden pulleys and black ropes along the side of a ship.

presets.title: Gryce
presets.author: Edith Wharton
presets.quote: “Like a merchant whose warehouses are crammed with an unmarketable commodity.”
presets.alt: Young man in a formal dark period suit standing in an ornate, warmly lit interior.

presets.title: Mattie
presets.author: Edith Wharton
presets.quote: “She was quick to learn, but forgetful and dreamy.”
presets.alt: Smiling woman in a pale blouse and flowing pink skirt walking through a sunlit grassy field.

presets.title: Olenska
presets.author: Edith Wharton
presets.quote: “She came rather late, one hand still ungloved, and fastening a bracelet about her wrist.”
presets.alt: Woman in a pale lace dress and large feathered hat looking to the side in a softly lit interior.

presets.title: Tintagel
presets.author: Edith Wharton
presets.quote: “The long murmur of the past breaking on the shores of a sleeping world.”
presets.alt: Three women in elaborate pale period gowns and hats seated beside a wooded lake with flower baskets.

presets.title: Violet
presets.author: Edith Wharton
presets.quote: “A harmless vampire in pearls who sought only to feed on the notoriety which all her millions could not create for her.”
presets.alt: Elegant woman in a gray fur coat and turban standing beside a green train as a porter carries vintage luggage.

poets-1.title: Poets Collection I
poets-1.description: A lyrical collection of presets inspired by the imagery, rhythm, and emotional landscapes of Emily Dickinson, William Carlos Williams, Phillis Wheatley, and Walt Whitman.
poets-1.menuImageAlt: A menu card representing Poets Collection I.

presets.title: Amber Hand
presets.author: Emily Dickinson
presets.quote: “She leads Him – docile as a Boy –along appointed Sands”
presets.quotefrom: The Moon Is Distant from the Sea
presets.alt: Full moon glowing above the dark silhouettes of bare tree branches.

presets.title: Gossamer
presets.author: Emily Dickinson
presets.quote: “The Carriage held but just Ourselves –and Immortality”
presets.quotefrom: Because I Could Not Stop for Death
presets.alt: Horse-drawn hearse standing among gravestones in a foggy cemetery.

presets.title: Pompeii
presets.author: Emily Dickinson
presets.quote: “phlegmatic mountains usually so still”
presets.alt: Volcano releasing a tall plume of smoke above a green forest and winding river.

presets.title: Stillness
presets.author: Emily Dickinson
presets.quote: “And then the Windows failed - and then I could not see to see”
presets.quotefrom: I Heard a Fly Buzz When I Died
presets.alt: Extreme close-up of a fly resting on a smooth blue surface.

presets.title: Velvet Masonry
presets.author: Emily Dickinson
presets.quote: “Like trains of cars on tracks of plush.”
presets.alt: Close-up of several honeybees crawling across dark, weathered wood.

presets.title: Black-Winged
presets.author: William Carlos Williams
presets.quote: “Hurl of the waters’ futile might!”
presets.alt: White gull with black-tipped wings flying against a cloudy blue sky.

presets.title: Glazed
presets.author: William Carlos Williams
presets.quote: “So much depends upon”
presets.alt: Black-and-white rooster and hen standing in grass beside a red wheelbarrow.

presets.title: Green Bottle
presets.author: William Carlos Williams
presets.quote: “The back wings of the hospital where nothing will grow”
presets.alt: Shattered pieces of green glass scattered across sandy ground.

presets.title: Lonely
presets.author: William Carlos Williams
presets.quote: “Who shall say I am not the happy genius of my household?”
presets.alt: Weathered white farmhouse at the end of a muddy road in dense fog.

presets.title: So Sweet
presets.author: William Carlos Williams
presets.quote: “Forgive me/they were delicious.”
presets.alt: Bowl filled with dark purple plums and green leaves beside a sunlit window.

presets.title: Aurora
presets.author: Phillis Wheatley
presets.quote: “Through all the heav'ns what beauteous dies are spread!”
presets.alt: Green northern lights and stars above snowy mountains and dark water beneath a low moon.

presets.title: Auspicious Queen
presets.author: Phillis Wheatley
presets.quote: “Arrayed in glory from the orbs above.”
presets.alt: Close side-profile of a woman beside a window, with her softly lit reflection in the glass.

presets.title: Avis
presets.author: Phillis Wheatley
presets.quote: “She feeds on truth and uncreated things.”
presets.alt: Single pale rose blooming against a dark, softly blurred background.

presets.title: Fancy
presets.author: Phillis Wheatley
presets.quote: “The fields may flourish, and gay scenes arise.”
presets.alt: Black man in Victorian mourning clothes seated between two young girls in a cemetery.

presets.title: Radiant Hinges
presets.author: Phillis Wheatley
presets.quote: “On what seraphic pinions shall we move, and view the landscapes in the realms above?”
presets.alt: Young Black boy reclining in a sunlit field with a horse-drawn carriage in the distance.

presets.title: Body Electric
presets.author: Walt Whitman
presets.quote: “O I say these are not the parts and poems of the body only, but of the soul.”
presets.alt: Four silhouetted people splashing in shallow ocean water beneath bright sunlight.

presets.title: Filament
presets.author: Walt Whitman
presets.quote: “Till the bridge you will need be form’d, till the ductile anchor hold.”
presets.alt: Orange-legged spider centered on its web against a dark background.

presets.title: Foray
presets.author: Walt Whitman
presets.quote:
“Arm'd and fearless—eating, drinking, sleeping, loving,
No law less than ourselves owning.”
presets.alt: Close-up of two people holding hands while walking side by side.

presets.title: Sprig
presets.author: Walt Whitman
presets.quote: “And what shall my perfume be for the grave of him I love?”
presets.quotefrom: When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d
presets.alt: Cluster of pink hydrangea blossoms growing beside a wooden picket fence.

presets.title: Varied Carols
presets.author: Walt Whitman
presets.quote: “Each singing what belongs to him or her and to none else.”
presets.alt: Cropped portrait of a mustached laborer wearing a work shirt and suspenders.

southern_drunks.title: Southern Drunks
southern_drunks.description: A richly cinematic collection inspired by the heat, humor, longing, and Gothic atmosphere of Truman Capote, William Faulkner, O. Henry, and Tennessee Williams.
southern_drunks.menuImageAlt: A menu card representing the Southern Drunks collection.

presets.title: Clutter
presets.author: Truman Capote
presets.quote: “Now, on this final day of her life, Mrs. Clutter hung in the closet the calico housedress she had been wearing.”
presets.alt: Large white farmhouse with a wraparound porch on a broad green lawn beneath billowing clouds.

presets.title: Golightly
presets.author: Truman Capote
presets.quote: “For all her chic thinness, she had an almost breakfast-cereal air of health, a soap and lemon cleanness.”
presets.alt: Row of ornate brownstone homes and stoops along a sunlit, tree-lined city street.

presets.title: Skully
presets.author: Truman Capote
presets.quote: “The shape of loneliness, greenly iridescent, whitely indefinite, seemed to rise from the garden.”
presets.alt: Old two-story house framed by sprawling oak trees draped in Spanish moss.

presets.title: Sook
presets.author: Truman Capote
presets.quote: “We're both quite awed at the prospect of drinking straight whiskey; the taste of it brings screwed-up expressions and sour shudders.”
presets.alt: Bottle of amber liquor on a rustic wooden floor beside a large wooden barrel.

presets.title: Talbo
presets.author: Truman Capote
presets.quote: “She had the eyes of a gifted person, kindled, transparent eyes, luminously green as mint jelly.”
presets.alt: Wooden treehouse with a ladder nestled among sunlit green branches.

presets.title: Addie
presets.author: William Faulkner
presets.quote:
“I could just remember how my father used to say that the reason for living
was to get ready to stay dead a long time.”
presets.alt: Weathered wooden wagon loaded with logs in an autumn woodland.

presets.title: Hogganbeck
presets.author: William Faulkner
presets.quote: “The motor vehicle was an insolvent phenomenon like last night's toadstool and, like the fungus, would vanish with tomorrow's sun.”
presets.alt: Dark vintage automobile parked in front of a wooden barn.

presets.title: Homer
presets.author: William Faulkner
presets.quote: “A thin, acrid pall as of the tomb seemed to lie everywhere upon this room decked and furnished as for a bridal.”
presets.alt: Decaying corpse in ornate clothing lying among red roses in a dark setting.

presets.title: Lena
presets.author: William Faulkner
presets.quote: “She expels her breath. It is not a sigh so much as a peaceful expiration, as though of peaceful astonishment.”
presets.alt: Red dirt road running between fenced green fields and bare trees beneath a misty sky.

presets.title: Snopes
presets.author: William Faulkner
presets.quote: “His father, still in the hat and coat, at once formal and burlesque as though dressed carefully for some shabby and ceremonial violence.”
presets.alt: Wooden barn engulfed in flames at night, sending thick smoke into the sky.

presets.title: Behrman
presets.author: O. Henry
presets.quote: “He had always talked of painting a great picture, a masterpiece, but he had never yet started it.”
presets.alt: Green ivy vines spreading across a cracked and weathered gray wall.

presets.title: Billy Jackson
presets.author: O. Henry
presets.quote: “I know as much as any of them about the style of sleeves they're going to wear next fall in Mars.”
presets.alt: View looking upward through a narrow enclosed courtyard toward a cloudy blue sky.

presets.title: Christmas
presets.author: O. Henry
presets.quote: “She stood by the window and looked out dully at a grey cat walking a grey fence in a grey backyard.”
presets.alt: Open metal scissors and a vintage pocket watch lying on a worn wooden surface.

presets.title: Hetty
presets.author: O. Henry
presets.quote: “Homely of countenance, with small, contemptuous, green eyes and chocolate-colored hair.”
presets.alt: Coiled sausage cooking on a grate beside a black cast-iron pot over an outdoor fire.

presets.title: Johnny
presets.author: O. Henry
presets.quote: “He started up a howl like a calliope and fastened himself as tight as a leech to Bill's leg.”
presets.alt: Young boy in a flat cap and brown suit sorting piles of coins.

presets.title: Alma
presets.author: Tennessee Williams
presets.quote: “Sometimes, out of necessity, we shadowy people take on a strength of our own. I have that now.”
presets.alt: Woman in an ornate white lace period dress standing in a brightly lit doorway.

presets.title: Cabeza de Lobo
presets.author: Tennessee Williams
presets.quote: “The steep white street in the sun that was like a great white bone of a giant beast that had caught on fire in the sky.”
presets.alt: Towering golden stone castle viewed from below against a vivid blue sky.

presets.title: Dubois
presets.author: Tennessee Williams
presets.quote: “It brought me here. Where I'm not wanted and where I'm ashamed to be.”
presets.alt: St. Charles streetcar approaching along wet tracks beneath a canopy of trees.

presets.title: Mendacity
presets.author: Tennessee Williams
presets.quote: “I have just now returned from the other side of the moon, death's country, son, and I'm not easy to shock by anything here.”
presets.quotefrom: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
presets.alt: Two-story white plantation-style house framed by oak branches draped in Spanish moss.

presets.title: Nightingale
presets.author: Tennessee Williams
presets.quote: “I don’t receive apparitions. They’re only seen by the mad.”
presets.alt: Empty street lined with colorful historic brick buildings, balconies, and black gas lamps.
